project.meaning: Something a community builds together on Homeroom: an app with its own page, chat and history.

community.meaning: The people a project belongs to; what a person joins.

proposal.meaning: A finished change put to the community's vote before it merges.

request.meaning: A feature idea or bug report filed on a project's board.

change.meaning: A piece of work on a project's code, from first draft to merge.

plan.meaning: What a change will do and how, written before it is built so the community can read it.

vote.meaning: A member's yes or no on a proposal or request (noun).

merge.meaning: Bring an approved change into the live project (verb).

preview.meaning: A running test copy of a project with a change applied.

checks.meaning: The automated tests a proposal must pass before it can merge.

member.meaning: A person who has joined a community.

Workshop.meaning: Name of the project page's tab where changes are built and reviewed.

Needs you.meaning: Name of the tab and feed listing the decisions waiting on the reader.

style.id: Indonesian as popular consumer apps write it: friendly and natural, addressing the reader as "kamu". Avoid stiff bureaucratic register and avoid needless English loanwords where a common Indonesian word exists.
style.es: Neutral Spanish that reads naturally across Latin America and Spain, addressing the reader as "tú". Avoid region-only vocabulary.
style.fr: French addressing the reader as "vous", concise as in a polished mobile app. Follow French typography: a narrow no-break space before ; ! ? and a no-break space before :, and « » for quotations.
style.pt-BR: Brazilian Portuguese addressing the reader as "você", friendly and concise as in a polished mobile app.
style.vi: Natural, concise Vietnamese addressing the reader as "bạn", as in a polished mobile app.
style.tr: Turkish addressing the reader as "sen", friendly and concise as in a polished mobile app. Follow Turkish capitalisation (i/İ, ı/I).
style.ru: Russian addressing the reader as "вы" (lowercase), concise as in a polished mobile app. Use « » for quotations and write ё where it belongs.
style.ar: Modern Standard Arabic, clear and friendly as in a polished mobile app. Prefer phrasing that avoids gendered verb forms where it reads naturally. Use Arabic punctuation (، ؛ ؟).
style.hi: Everyday Hindi in Devanagari as popular Indian apps write it, addressing the reader as "आप". Keep common English tech words people already use (such as ऐप, लॉग इन) rather than rare Sanskritised terms. End sentences with ।.
style.zh-CN: Simplified Chinese as polished mainland apps write it: concise and friendly, addressing the reader as "你". Use full-width punctuation (，。：？！) and “ ” for quotations, with no spaces between Chinese characters.
style.ja: Polite Japanese (です/ます) as polished Japanese apps write it, with short noun or plain-form labels on buttons. Use full-width punctuation (、。) and 「」 for quotations, with no spaces between Japanese words.
style.ko: Polite Korean (해요체) as popular Korean apps write it, concise on buttons, with standard Korean spacing.
